Class RequestPredicates

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.web.router.builder.RequestPredicates
public final class RequestPredicates extends Object
Shorthands of RouteCondition for RouteSpec.where(RouteCondition) and RouteSpec.where(RouteCondition): conditions on the headers, query parameters, accepted media types, content type and method of a request. Each returns a RouteCondition, so they combine with RouteCondition.and(RouteCondition), RouteCondition.or(RouteCondition) and RouteCondition.negate(), with lambdas made conditions with RouteCondition.custom(Predicate), or with all(RouteCondition...) and any(RouteCondition...). 
import static io.micronaut.web.router.builder.RequestPredicates.*;

routes.GET("/reports/{id}")
    .where(queryParam("format", "csv").or(accept(MediaType.of("text/csv"))))
    .handle(csvHandler);
routes.path("/beta", beta -> {
    beta.where(header("X-Beta", value -> value.equals("on")));
    beta.GET("/search", betaSearchHandler);
});

The URI, the method, the media types a route consumes and produces, and the @RouteCondition expression of an annotated method are conditions of their own, which also decide the 405, 415 and 406 answers. A condition of where does not: a request it rejects is answered as if the route did not exist. Use accept(MediaType...) and contentType(MediaType...) to choose among routes that consume or produce the same media types by another criterion, not to replace RouteSpec.consumes(MediaType...) or RouteSpec.produces(MediaType...).

accept(MediaType...) and contentType(MediaType...) compare media types, with the wildcards of either side, and read the list of the Accept header, in which a request without the header accepts every type: they are RouteCondition.Custom conditions, since a matcher of the string of a header does not express that. So is a condition that takes a lambda of a value.

    • accept

      public static RouteCondition accept(MediaType... mediaTypes)
      A request that accepts one of the media types: a type of its Accept header is compatible with one of them, e.g. text/* with text/csv. A request without an Accept header accepts every type.
      Parameters:
      mediaTypes - The media types
      Returns:
      The condition, a RouteCondition.Custom one

    • contentType

      public static RouteCondition contentType(MediaType... mediaTypes)
      A request whose content type is compatible with one of the media types, e.g. application/* with application/json. A request without a content type does not meet the condition.
      Parameters:
      mediaTypes - The media types
      Returns:
      The condition, a RouteCondition.Custom one

    • method

      public static RouteCondition method(HttpMethod... methods)
      A request of one of the HTTP methods, e.g. for the routes of a group, or of a route of several methods: group.where(method(HttpMethod.GET).or(header("X-Write-Token"))). A custom method is HttpMethod.CUSTOM.
      Parameters:
      methods - The methods
      Returns:
      The condition
      See Also:
      • RouteCondition.method(HttpMethod...)

    • all

      public static RouteCondition all(RouteCondition... conditions)
      A request that meets every condition. The router evaluates them cheapest first until one is not met, the lambdas last, in order.
      Parameters:
      conditions - The conditions, see RouteCondition.custom(Predicate) for a lambda
      Returns:
      The condition, met by every request if there are none

    • any

      public static RouteCondition any(RouteCondition... conditions)
      A request that meets one of the conditions. The router evaluates them cheapest first until one is met, the lambdas last, in order.
      Parameters:
      conditions - The conditions, see RouteCondition.custom(Predicate) for a lambda
      Returns:
      The condition, met by no request if there are none
